title: [R3-12] Refuse a forged pnpm on the Windows release path
description:
FILED FROM THE THIRD HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #3 (anchored d01c3316, 2026-08-28: 'Request changes - do not merge', 12 P1 merge blockers + P2 follow-ups). Re-verified at HEAD a09b11fa by a read-only verifier; see the ruling memo in the epic channel. Reviewer's finding: R3-12 forged pnpm attestation. Existing rows checked: task-bd7d612fd1be49b4b88a3e75715762f3(DONE) closesIt=false, task-c289b8fbcb9840968a9b3994e73b79a4(BLOCKED) closesIt=false, task-78b0c2f65c9a4962b6b62030f83ffa1c(WORKING) closesIt=false, task-34788b67ad61420bb549821fe7cb39ad(DONE) closesIt=false. Gap this row closes: No open or closed row authenticates the bytes of the pnpm tree that the release path executes, and no row moves the ZIP-producing step (and release:evidence) off the ambient `pnpm` shim onto a directly invoked, independently authenticated Node. Searches for forged pnpm, pnpm attestation, pnpm tree authenticate, pnpm runner identity, pack:windows entrypoint, d01c3316, third review, R3-12 all return zero rows; the 301 hits for "pnpm" contain only P2.16 and the ENOENT row in this class. The inner packer's tree/node digests (pack-command.ts:26-29) exist but are unreachable from the workflow's trust path because the workflow enters through `pnpm pack:windows` and the packer trusts `npm_execpath`.

P1 merge blocker R3-12 from the third human review of PR #3 (anchored at d01c3316), re-measured at HEAD a09b11fa: STILL PRESENT, no fixing commit.

REVIEWER MECHANISM (verbatim intent): the pnpm runner verifies location, filename, manifest name/version and bin mapping, not package-tree or entrypoint bytes (scripts/release/pnpm-runner.mjs:94-167). A fake pnpm@11.0.8 was accepted by production resolution and executed FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED. The candidate workflow runs a lifecycle-enabled install, then invokes `pnpm pack:windows` through this ambient installation; a substituted pnpm bypasses the hardened inner packer, creates an arbitrary ZIP, and downstream jobs attest those bytes. Required: authenticate the complete pnpm tree and invoke critical tracked Node entrypoints directly through independently authenticated Node.

HEAD RE-MEASURE (a09b11fa):
- scripts/release/pnpm-runner.mjs is byte-identical to d01c3316 (empty `git log d01c3316..HEAD -- <path>`). verifiedIdentity :99-110 = realpath equality (:101-102), escapesRoot (:103-104), lstat isFile (:105), manifest name/version (:106-107), bin mapping (:108). No createHash anywhere. runActionPnpm :163 re-runs that same identity check, then :165 spawns `process.execPath [entry, ...args]`. refuse() :34 answers TOOLCHAIN_OBSERVATION_FAILED for everything; TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH (release-subject.mjs:34) is in the frozen vocabulary and unused.
- The suite accepts a forged tree by construction: actionLayout() in tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs writes {name:"pnpm", version:PNPM_PIN, bin:{pnpm:"bin/pnpm.cjs"}} plus a one-line `#!/usr/bin/env node` entry; the arm at :1162-1172 asserts launch.ok === true on it. The reviewer's fake pnpm is this fixture with a body.
- .github/workflows/reusable-windows-candidate-build.yml (391 lines; ceiling 400 at tests/integration/release/release-workflow-contract.test.ts:202): :92 pnpm/action-setup 11.0.8 -> :124 `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (no --ignore-scripts; no .npmrc at HEAD; pnpm-workspace.yaml has no onlyBuiltDependencies; package.json has no pnpm key; no workspace package declares preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare) -> :131-:230 every gate via bare `pnpm <script>`, including :230 `pnpm release:evidence` which is scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:87 resolveActionPnpm + :93/:311 frozenInstall through the same tree -> :336 `pnpm pack:windows` via the ambient PATH shim -> :342 `node scripts/release/windows-pack-observation.mjs create --artifact dist/moe-windows.zip` observes whatever bytes are in dist. Nothing between :92 and :342 re-authenticates the pnpm tree.
- The inner packer already owns an authenticated-toolchain pattern: tools/packaging/pack-command.ts:26-29 pins EXACT_NODE_VERSION v24.16.0, NODE_NATIVE_SHA256, PNPM_NATIVE_SHA256, PNPM_PACKAGE_TREE_SHA256; resolvePnpmPackTool :192-259 digests the whole package tree via capturePackTreeIdentity (tools/packaging/pack-tool-identity.ts:129-170, sorted relative paths, kind/size/sha256 per entry) and normalizedTreeSha256 (:160-169); resolveWindowsPackToolchain :274-289 digests node.exe. But :200 takes the pnpm root from `npm_execpath`, i.e. from whichever pnpm invoked the packer, and the workflow only ever enters through that pnpm, so a forged pnpm never calls the packer at all. pack-windows.ts:209-222 shows the packer's own pnpm use (install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts, deploy) already goes through the digested tool.
- Downstream: scripts/release/verify-windows-release.mjs:243-263 binds provenance receipt <-> zip byteLength/sha256 only; nothing binds the zip to a packer toolchain receipt. publish-windows-release.yml:212 actions/attest subject-path is moe-windows.zip. The reviewer's claim that the forged bytes get attested is confirmed.

WHAT CLOSES IT: (1) pnpm-runner.mjs authenticates the complete `<PNPM_HOME>/../pnpm` tree bytes against the one pinned digest, at resolution and again immediately before spawn, answering TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH; (2) the workflow's ZIP-producing step and release:evidence step invoke the tracked entrypoints directly through a node whose version and SHA-256 are verified against the same pinned constants the packer uses, never through `pnpm pack:windows`; (3) the packer accepts the action handoff (PNPM_HOME layout + tree digest) when `npm_execpath` is absent, because `npm_execpath` is itself trust in the invoking pnpm.
definitionOfDone: RUNNER TREE AUTHENTICATION: resolveActionPnpm and the pre-spawn re-check in runActionPnpm (scripts/release/pnpm-runner.mjs) compute the normalized SHA-256 of the complete `<PNPM_HOME>/../pnpm` package tree (same normalization as tools/packaging/pack-tool-identity.ts capturePackTreeIdentity + pack-command.ts normalizedTreeSha256: sorted relative path, kind, size, per-file sha256, symlink = refuse) and compare it to ONE pinned constant shared with pack-command.ts PNPM_PACKAGE_TREE_SHA256; a mismatch answers releaseRefusal("TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH") and never spawns. Drill R3-12-A (the reviewer's reproduction): an action-layout tree with correct manifest name/version/bin whose entry writes FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED -> resolve refuses with TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, an exec spy on runActionPnpm records 0 calls, and FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED appears in no stream. Drill R3-12-B (one degree of freedom): flip one byte in a NON-entry file of an otherwise-accepted tree -> refused; restore -> accepte

SWAP WINDOW: a tree replaced after resolveActionPnpm returned ok and before runActionPnpm spawns is refused by the pre-spawn re-digest (the existing :95-97 window guarantee now covers bytes, not just identity). Drill R3-12-D: resolve a genuine tree, overwrite one file with different bytes of equal length and equal mtime, call runActionPnpm -> exitCode 1, exec spy 0 calls; restore the bytes -> the same descriptor spawns once.

DIRECT AUTHENTICATED NODE INVOCATION: in .github/workflows/reusable-windows-candidate-build.yml the ZIP-producing step (:336 today) and the release-evidence step (:230 today) no longer run `pnpm pack:windows` / `pnpm release:evidence`; each resolves node from the setup-node install, verifies `--version` === v24.16.0 and Get-FileHash SHA256 === NODE_NATIVE_SHA256 (the same values pack-command.ts:26-27 pins; one source of truth, e.g. a tracked JSON the step and the packer both read), then runs `node tools/packaging/pack-windows-main.ts` / `node scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs --head` directly with shell-free argv; the packer's resolvePnpmPackTool accepts the PNPM_HOME action layout with the tree digest when npm_execpath is absent. Drill R3-12-E: the workflow contract test (release-workflow-contract.test.ts or verify-windows-release.test.mjs, whichever already parses this file) reds by name when :336 is restored to `run: pnpm pack:windows`, reds when the SHA256 comparison is deleted from

END-TO-END FORGERY REPRODUCTION: a node:test harness (tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs or a sibling under tests/integration/release/) stages a forged pnpm@11.0.8 at PNPM_HOME AND first on PATH, runs the workflow's pack-step shape locally against a temp repository copy, and asserts dist/moe-windows.zip is absent (or the step exits nonzero with the refusal code) and FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED is absent from stdout/stderr/filesystem. Drill R3-12-F (harness can fail): with the runner digest check reverted in a %TEMP% copy of the tree, the identical harness produces the forged ZIP -> the arm is red; restore -> green.

GATES AND EVIDENCE: standalone runs with exit codes and count lines recorded in a row comment: `pnpm typecheck:release`; `node --test tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` (nonzero counts, the existing 29-drill runner arms still green or explicitly migrated to the injected-digest form, none deleted); `pnpm exec vitest run tools/packaging/pack-command.test.ts tests/integration/release/release-workflow-contract.test.ts`; `node --test tests/integration/release/verify-windows-release.test.mjs`; repo-wide `pnpm test` path-attributed. Every drill above carries a restore proof (SHA256 equal on the owned path, `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` or `git diff --no-index` against the %TEMP% backup). Explicit-pathspec commit of owned paths only; the row comment names the reviewer finding R3-12 and d01c3316 and states how the pinned pnpm tree digest was derived (pnpm@11.0.8 registry tarball integrity -> action-setup layout).
taskRails: P1 merge blocker from the third human review of PR #3 (anchor d01c3316); never soften the reviewer's claim without a measurement that contradicts it. Re-measure pnpm-runner.mjs:99-110 and reusable-windows-candidate-build.yml:124/:230/:336 at claim time: HEAD moves (146+ commits since the anchor already).

OWNERSHIP: adopt P2.16 (task-bd7d612f, DONE) and its runner suite; do not reopen it. task-78b0c2f6 (WORKING) holds reusable-windows-candidate-build.yml dirty with ` # vX.Y.Z` comments and its DoD requires clean porcelain on that path: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK on it landing first, or coordinate in chat; never regenerate the workflow from a HEAD copy (peer-WIP destruction). cross-host.yml belongs to task-24e066557 and is not the attested release path: out of scope here.

LINE CAPS: tools/packaging/pack-command.ts is already 406 lines (over the 400 production cap) - do not grow it; put any shared digest helper in pack-tool-identity.ts (~190 lines) or a new module with its .js bridge (new TS modules need a bridge invisible to tsc and vitest). pnpm-runner.mjs is 179 lines. The workflow is 391/400 (release-workflow-contract.test.ts:202): budget every added step line.

ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH for NODE_NATIVE_SHA256 / EXACT_NODE_VERSION / PNPM_PACKAGE_TREE_SHA256 consumed by the packer, the runner and the workflow step; tests compare against literal hex or an injected expected digest, never the constant imported from the module under test (fixed-point fixture). Production call sites pass no override - assert it.

Keep the runner's contract: shell:false, spawn `process.execPath [entry]`, never execute the shim, never a PATH fallback; structural failures keep TOOLCHAIN_OBSERVATION_FAILED, digest mismatch uses TOOLCHAIN_IDENTITY_MISMATCH - both already in release-subject.mjs:34, add no new codes; no path, environment value or raw child error may leak in a refusal.

The existing actionLayout fixture IS a forged tree: arms that expect acceptance migrate to the injected-digest form; do not relax the digest to make them pass and do not delete drills from the 29-drill P2.16 sheet.

Windows discipline: drill backups in %TEMP% not /tmp; PowerShell restore can silently no-op - prove restore with a hash compare; Get-FileHash and node:crypto must agree on the same bytes (drill the disagreement once).

OUT OF SCOPE unless the architect measures otherwise: changing the :124 install's lifecycle policy (no --ignore-scripts today; the packer's own install already uses --ignore-scripts at pack-windows.ts:210); a packer-toolchain receipt inside the ZIP bound by verify-windows-release.mjs (note it as a follow-up if not taken).
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure the cited lines at claim time; if a sibling row landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.
